parsed.attack: The audience is parents of under-fives, whose calendar free/busy is fiction - the 2pm gap is a nap that failed - so by the fourth or fifth brief where the named 'callable window' was not actually callable, the forty-second brief becomes the thing swiped off the lock screen unread. Nothing at all is lost by ignoring it: the product accumulates no state, keeps no record of calls made, produces no artifact, so cancelling at the first renewal costs the user precisely nothing, which is the profile of a 1.4% retainer. 'Habit_lock' as the moat on a daily digest is the claim under test, not a reply to it.
parsed.strongest_defence: The overlap arithmetic is real work the person cannot do in their head and the platform genuinely hands it over, so the brief is right about a fact rather than nagging about a feeling - the failure named in the evidence is the hour, and this fixes the hour. Decaying opens are fixed by firing rarely: deliver only on days when the overlap is unusually good, which turns a daily digest into occasional news, and freemium needs only the 3% for whom the window was right.
parsed.verdict_reason: A daily prompt with zero accumulating state, computed from a free/busy signal that is systematically wrong for this audience, trains dismissal inside the first week and leaves nothing to defend at renewal - and the only defence that works, firing rarely on unusual overlaps, is a different product with a different cadence.
